question: Can the unchanged frozen B001 learned planner execute on spare CPUs with stable candidate costs and practical runtime before deciding whether to move its already-planned baseline evaluations to CPU?
hypothesis: The final reviewed float64/math baseline may permit CPU planning without changing tasks or optimizer behavior; this must be measured rather than inferred from inexpensive physical probes.

sources.sections: Section4.4 terminal latent-goal planning and section5.1.1 evaluation
sources.consequence: Evaluate planning directly rather than infer it from probe accuracy. Keep existing B001 tasks, cost and CEM settings; a tiny runtime case cannot estimate success rate.

sources.sections: AppendixG cost and CEM final elite mean
sources.consequence: Preserve final elite-mean action selection. The local B001 horizon/candidate/iteration settings differ from this paper and remain frozen; do not adopt new settings for speed.

sources.sections: Floating-point platform differences, batched versus sliced computations and finite values
sources.consequence: Check actual100-candidate/eight-step CPU costs against singleton subsets and reversed order at existing tolerances. CPU/GPU bitwise equivalence and identical CEM elite choices are not guaranteed.

sources.sections: Popen timeout cleanup and confirmed returncode
sources.consequence: Use reviewed owned-child termination with a180second CPU cap including15second cleanup; signal only that child, never the live GPU trainer.

sources.sections: Inputs, task_start, task_inputs, cem and learned_actions
sources.consequence: Import unchanged task selection and learned_actions. Construct a separate fixed-cost numerical diagnostic without altering the real planner. Do not call its GPU admission harness.

differences: A CPU feasibility diagnostic only, using the existing final L0n3seed0 calibrated artifact. No training, calibration, dataset collection, test-driven tuning or full success-rate claim. B001 currently runs learned planning on GPU; any later full CPU execution requires an explicit new record after this result review.
contrary_evidence: Planning calls a neural rollout many more times than probes. Good probe accuracy does not establish latent-goal planning, and small numerical changes can change elite ranking. A single episode gives a weak runtime estimate and no general success estimate. CPU work could contend with a GPU trainer for host resources.

protocol.parents: Require passing actual A003/A015/A016 final L0n3seed0 reviews, step303000, calibrated float64/math metadata, existing n3 B001 controls and exact test data hashes inherited from reviewed C006. Bind source and inputs; keep live GATED checkout untouched.
protocol.case: Only n3seed0 L0 test episode0. Run unchanged learned_actions at H4,H6,H8, then repeat H8 with identical CEM seed. Keep100 candidates,10 elites,20 iterations,std2,cap3,floor0.001,three history frames,two historical actions and independently encoded goal.
protocol.numerics: At H8 first CEM proposal batch, compute terminal predicted latents and squared goal costs for all100 candidates, first8 singleton candidates and reversed100 ordering. Compare at rtol1e-4,atol1e-5; check finite CPU tensors, all parameters/buffers unchanged and no CUDA initialization. Repeat H8 actions at the same tolerance. No GPU calls or GPU parity claim.
protocol.feasibility: Report each planner latency and sum(H4,H6,H8)*1000 as a rough full-model estimate. CPU full evaluation is eligible for a separately preregistered implementation only if all checks pass and estimate<=6900seconds (prospective7200second per-model cap). Do not alter thread count, planner parameters or case selection in response to results. Failing the estimate returns evaluation to the existing sequential GPU plan.
protocol.software_checks: Check all1000 episode/horizon task bounds; exact history/past/goal indexing using distinct synthetic frame values; recording fake CPU model confirms independent goal encoding,20 batches of100 proposals, preserved two historical actions, finite/capped deterministic final actions and no future observation access. Check hidden-device/nonfinite guards and exact reviewed lineage/source bindings.
protocol.execution: One CPU child, eight Torch/OMP/BLAS threads and one interop thread, hidden HIP/CUDA/ROCR, RSS<=16GiB. Software cap60seconds, actual preflight180seconds including15seconds cleanup. File logs and immutable new outputs; reuse exact reviewed A016 stop helper. No GPU ledger interval. Inspect and literature-review raw and operational results separately; no automatic approval or full evaluation.
protocol.outputs: outputs/gated/B002/software and preflight_l0_n3_s0, with exact models/data/sources/reviews in manifest, sampled proposal diagnostic, actions, latency and limits. Do not write a canonical planning/RUN result or fill C002 performance cells from this tiny diagnostic.

success: Scoped software checks and actual numerical/immutability/CPU checks pass; runtime eligibility is reported separately. Neither outcome establishes planning success or robot transfer.
stop: Stop on stale lineage, invalid numerics, CPU limits or device initialization. Preserve partial technical or budget-incomplete evidence. Do not change active GPU training, scientific source, precision, tolerances, test task or CEM settings.
